newsitem.title: USA: Second-hand smoke doubles heart risk - study.
newsitem.headline: Second-hand smoke doubles heart risk - study.

text.p: Women who do not smoke but are exposed regularly to other people's cigarette smoke are twice as likely to develop coronary heart disease as those who are not exposed, according to a study published on Tuesday.

In the study in the latest issue of Circulation, a journal published by the American Heart Association, Harvard University researchers also found that the increase in risk associated with exposure at home is substantially the same as risk associated with exposure at work.
Their data came from the Nurses' Health Study, a study of 121,700 female registered nurses aged 30 to 55 who provided information on their diet, lifestyle and health since 1976.
Some 32,046 of the studied women were nonsmokers and provided information about their exposure to smoke from others, at home and at work.
The researchers from Harvard's School of Public Health and Medical School controlled conditions that might contribute to heart disease, such as hypertension, diet and exercise.
"We were startled by the strength of these findings," Dr. Ichiro Kawachi, the study's lead author said.
"The strong association we have found suggests that as many as 30,000 to 60,000 deaths each year from coronary heart disease could be attributable to passive smoke."
The researchers said their findings applied equally to men and women.
